title: The extension-by-zero presheaf of a module on a localized ringed site
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a site, $\mathcal O$ a sheaf of rings on $\mathcal C$, $U$ an object of $\mathcal C$, and $(\mathcal C/U,\mathcal O_U)$ the localized ringed site with $\mathcal O_U(V\xrightarrow{\varphi}U)=\mathcal O(V)$ [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]. For a sheaf $\mathcal G$ of $\mathcal O_U$-modules on $\mathcal C/U$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], the *extension-by-zero presheaf* $P_{\mathcal G}$ is the presheaf of $\mathcal O$-modules on $\mathcal C$
$$
 P_{\mathcal G}(V)=\bigoplus_{\varphi\in\mathrm{Mor}_{\mathcal C}(V,U)}\mathcal G(V\xrightarrow{\varphi}U),
$$
where $f\in\mathcal O(V)=\mathcal O_U(V\xrightarrow{\varphi}U)$ acts on the summand of $\varphi$ by the $\mathcal O_U$-module structure of $\mathcal G$, and where the restriction along $a:V'\to V$ sends $s$ in the summand of $\varphi$ to $s|_{V'}\in\mathcal G(V'\xrightarrow{\varphi a}U)$, its restriction in $\mathcal G$ along the morphism $a:(V',\varphi a)\to(V,\varphi)$ of $\mathcal C/U$, placed in the summand of $\varphi a$. A morphism $\alpha:\mathcal G\to\mathcal G'$ induces $P_\alpha$, acting by $\alpha_{(V,\varphi)}$ on the summand of $\varphi$; this is a functor from sheaves of $\mathcal O_U$-modules to presheaves of $\mathcal O$-modules. *Special case:* if every object $V$ has at most one morphism to $U$, then $P_{\mathcal G}(V)=\mathcal G(V\to U)$ when a morphism $V\to U$ exists and $P_{\mathcal G}(V)=0$ otherwise; the restriction along $V'\to V$ is that of $\mathcal G$ when $V$ maps to $U$ (then so does $V'$), and is the zero map otherwise.
